# CANDIDATE: VIX_TERM_STRUCTURE_LEVEL_BREAK_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the VIX term structure is in steep contango (VIX/VIX1D > 1.2), breakouts of prior‑day highs with above‑average volume tend to be reinforced by low near‑term volatility expectations. This edge exists because steep contango reflects market expectations of calmer near-term markets, reducing the probability of false breakouts and increasing the likelihood of sustained upward momentum.

## Mechanism

Compute ratio = VIX / VIX1D (both from options_structure_metrics) for the current 5‑min bar. If ratio > 1.2 and price breaks above the prior day’s high (PDH) on a 5‑min bar with volume > 1.5 × the average 5‑bar volume of the last 20 bars, enter long at the close of that breakout bar. Exit: Stop at the mid‑point between PDH and prior day’s low (PDL) or 0.5% below entry, whichever is tighter; take profit at 2× ATR(5) above entry, with a runner that trails 20% of HWM after 1.5× ATR profit. Regime hint: Ideal when VIX < 18 (low absolute volatility) and term structure ratio > 1.2; avoid during high‑impact news (e.g., CPI, FOMC) regardless of ratio.
